author: 奥玛·海亚姆
profile: 波斯数学家兼诗人，《鲁拜集》四行诗劝人把握当下、饮酒及时，带着对命运与死亡的清醒。适合及时行乐的人物信条、命运不可改写的旁白、酒宴场景的题眼。
source: 文本据 Edward FitzGerald 英译 Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam 第五版（1889），第 1 首另附第一版（1859）文本；译者 1883 年去世，英译为公有领域。只收英文原文。

entries.title: Rubaiyat 第 1 首（第五版）
entries.text:
Wake! For the Sun, who scatter'd into flight
The Stars before him from the Field of Night,
Drives Night along with them from Heav'n, and strikes
The Sultán's Turret with a Shaft of Light.
famous_lines: Wake! For the Sun, who scatter'd into flight
The Sultán's Turret with a Shaft of Light.
drama_uses: 新一天开始的转场旁白
entries.note: FitzGerald 第五版（1889）。 英文原文为公有领域；中译本多数仍在版权期，剧中使用请自行翻译或化用。

entries.title: Rubaiyat 第 1 首（第一版）
entries.text:
Awake! for Morning in the Bowl of Night
Has flung the Stone that puts the Stars to Flight:
And Lo! the Hunter of the East has caught
The Sultan's Turret in a Noose of Light.
famous_lines: Awake! for Morning in the Bowl of Night
Has flung the Stone that puts the Stars to Flight
entries.note: FitzGerald 第一版（1859）。 英文原文为公有领域；中译本多数仍在版权期，剧中使用请自行翻译或化用。

entries.title: Rubaiyat 第 7 首
entries.text:
Come, fill the Cup, and in the fire of Spring
Your Winter-garment of Repentance fling:
The Bird of Time has but a little way
To flutter—and the Bird is on the Wing.
famous_lines: Come, fill the Cup, and in the fire of Spring
The Bird of Time has but a little way To flutter—and the Bird is on the Wing.
drama_uses: 春天放下悔恨重新开始的旁白

entries.title: Rubaiyat 第 12 首
entries.text:
A Book of Verses underneath the Bough,
A Jug of Wine, a Loaf of Bread—and Thou
Beside me singing in the Wilderness—
Oh, Wilderness were Paradise enow!
famous_lines: A Book of Verses underneath the Bough
A Jug of Wine, a Loaf of Bread—and Thou
Oh, Wilderness were Paradise enow!
drama_uses: 恋人野餐树下的甜蜜段落
片名或集名：荒野即天堂

entries.title: Rubaiyat 第 24 首
entries.text:
Ah, make the most of what we yet may spend,
Before we too into the Dust descend;
Dust into Dust, and under Dust to lie,
Sans Wine, sans Song, sans Singer, and—sans End!
famous_lines: Ah, make the most of what we yet may spend
Before we too into the Dust descend
Sans Wine, sans Song, sans Singer, and—sans End!
drama_uses: 绝症人物决定尽情活一次的旁白

entries.title: Rubaiyat 第 27 首
entries.text:
Myself when young did eagerly frequent
Doctor and Saint, and heard great argument
About it and about: but evermore
Came out by the same door where in I went.
famous_lines: Myself when young did eagerly frequent Doctor and Saint
Came out by the same door where in I went.
drama_uses: 求学求道多年仍困惑的自嘲独白
中年人物回望青春的旁白

entries.title: Rubaiyat 第 29 首
entries.text:
Into this Universe, and Why not knowing
Nor Whence, like Water willy-nilly flowing;
And out of it, as Wind along the Waste,
I know not Whither, willy-nilly blowing.
famous_lines: Into this Universe, and Why not knowing
I know not Whither, willy-nilly blowing.
drama_uses: 人生从何来往何去的片头题眼

entries.title: Rubaiyat 第 71 首（命运之指）
entries.text:
The Moving Finger writes; and, having writ,
Moves on: nor all your Piety nor Wit
Shall lure it back to cancel half a Line,
Nor all your Tears wash out a Word of it.
famous_lines: The Moving Finger writes; and, having writ, Moves on
Nor all your Tears wash out a Word of it.
drama_uses: 无法挽回的错误铸成后的旁白
entries.note: FitzGerald 第五版（1889）第 71 首，第一版为第 51 首。 英文原文为公有领域；中译本多数仍在版权期，剧中使用请自行翻译或化用。

entries.title: Rubaiyat 第 99 首
entries.text:
Ah Love! could you and I with Him conspire
To grasp this sorry Scheme of Things entire,
Would not we shatter it to bits—and then
Re-mould it nearer to the Heart's Desire!
famous_lines: Ah Love! could you and I with Him conspire
Would not we shatter it to bits—and then Re-mould it nearer to the Heart's Desire!
drama_uses: 恋人誓言改写命运的台词
